name: sol_defi_as_10
description: AMM/pool fails to handle rebasing tokens, causing balance accounting mismatches
question: The source file in `source` implements an AMM or liquidity pool that tracks pooled token balances using cached/stored reserve variables (e.g. `reserve0`/`reserve1` or similar) updated only on deposit/withdraw/swap, without reconciling them against the token's live `balanceOf(address(this))`, so that a rebasing token's automatic balance increase or decrease desynchronizes the pool's internal accounting from its real token holdings, enabling stuck funds, incorrect swap pricing, or drainage of the mismatched balance; this excludes pools that explicitly disallow rebasing tokens via allowlists or that resync reserves to actual balanceOf before every accounting-sensitive operation.
criteria: swap() computes output amounts using stored reserve0/reserve1 state variables instead of calling balanceOf() on the pool's actual token holdings
addLiquidity()/removeLiquidity() mint or burn LP shares based on cached reserve variables that are never resynced with token.balanceOf(address(this))
_update() sets reserves directly from deposited/withdrawn amounts without querying the token's current real balance, ignoring rebasing-induced balance drift
the pool holds a rebasing token but computes user-owed amounts from a fixed recorded balance captured at deposit time rather than the token's live balance
